answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently checked tasks fail or duplicate claims are proven. Rewards are paid only after verification, so creating a thousand cedar or island-themed personas does not multiply influence: each must fund its own bond and earn a track record. A cipher can bind submissions to the bonded key, making identity swaps harder. The attacker pays capital costs, risks forfeiture, and must sustain credible work across identities.
